findings.title: Deferred cancellation misses reminders due before the next cron run
findings.body: Cancellation now only marks a scheduled email as cancelled, leaving SendGrid cancellation to this 15-minute cron job. If a booking is cancelled at 10:01 and its reminder is due at 10:10, SendGrid sends it before the next run at 10:15. That run also deletes the expired reminder record before querying cancellations, so it never attempts cancellation. Reminders close to their send time need immediate cancellation rather than relying exclusively on the cron job.

findings.title: Rescheduling bypasses the deferred cancellation mechanism
findings.body: Passing immediateDelete=true cancels the old email in SendGrid immediately, even when its send date is days away. These cancellations remain pending until their scheduled dates and consume the same 100-pending-cancellation quota described in this PR. Once the quota is exhausted, deleteScheduledEmailReminder catches the failure without marking the reminder cancelled, so the cron job cannot retry it and the old booking's reminder is sent. Rescheduling needs to persist cancellation intent and use the deferred mechanism too.

findings.title: Await reminder cancellation persistence before completing the request
findings.body: The cancellation helpers are asynchronous, but their returned promises are discarded by both nested forEach calls and are not included in the final Promise.all. Previously, deletion of the reminder records was awaited. The handler can now report successful cancellation while the cancelled flag or unscheduled-reminder deletion is still pending; in a serverless deployment, outstanding work can be suspended when the response finishes, leaving reminders eligible to send. Collect and await these promises before returning. The request-reschedule handler has the same issue.

findings.title: Isolate cancellation failures and commit each successful cancellation
findings.body: A single failed SendGrid request exits the entire cancellation loop, preventing every subsequent reminder from being cancelled in that run. Furthermore, the Prisma delete operations collected for earlier successful cancellations are lazy promises and are only executed by Promise.all after the loop; an exception skips that call, leaving all those records in the queue too. A persistently failing batch can therefore block other cancellations until their emails are sent. Handle errors per reminder and await deletion immediately after each successful cancellation.
